::: {.why}
The oldest signal in the literature, and the one where a point-in-time violation is easiest to make and most flattering to your results.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Construct book-to-market with the correct filing lag and say what the naive version would have gained you.
- Report the signal's IC and information ratio against the null on your own universe.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Build the signal in qlib/signals/value.py using the SEC financial statement data sets and the three-date schema from day 137, so book value enters only after its filing date. Compute book-to-market against the current market value on each rebalance.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [15 min]{.task-min} Measure what the lag costs: run the same signal with the correct lag and with book value applied from the fiscal period end rather than the filing date, and report both ICs. The difference is a pure look-ahead effect and it is a number worth remembering when reading other people's value replications.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Generate the signal page and compare its IC against the published estimates for the same period, noting where your universe and construction differ.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
Value joins the book as the first fundamental signal, built on the point-in-time filing schema, with the cost of getting the lag wrong measured rather than assumed.
:::
